newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat harvest hampered by rain, humidity.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat harvest hampered by rain, humidity.

text.p: Rain and high humidity caused combines to stay out of wheat fields in southwest Oklahoma during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.
"Harvest has started rather tentatively as high moisture content in test cuttings has kept producers out of fields," the service said in its weekly crop progress report.
The state's wheat was rated six percent very poor, 10 poor, 30 fair, 51 good and three percent excellent. A week ago, the crop was rated 12 percent very poor, 14 poor, 38 fair and 36 percent good.

Wheat was one percent harvested, against 25 percent last year and 11 on average. Seventy-nine percent of the wheat crop had reached the soft dough stage, versus 89 last year and 85 for the five-year average.
None of the state's corn was tasseling, against eight percent last year and six on average. Soybeans were 65 percent planted, against 77 last year and 51 percent on average.
Sorghum acreage was 24 percent planted, versus 52 percent last year and 56 percent on average.
Pasture and range conditions declined from the previous week and were rated nil very poor, two percent poor, 22 percent fair, 68 percent good and eight percent excellent.
